text:
maya: Heads-up: I pushed a quick experiment for SLO-aware packing. TL;DR: aggressive packing reduced p95 for short sequences but caused a tail spike on A100 when KV cache hit-rate dropped. Posting quick numbers and a config prototype below.

ranjit: Can you share the p50/p95/p99 deltas?

maya: Quick summary table I pulled from the run (all percent change vs current prod policy):
- L4: p95 -12%, p99 -5%
- T4: p95 -8%, p99 +2%
- A10: p95 -10%, p99 -1%
- A100: p95 +22%, p99 +40% (bad)
- H100: p95 -5%, p99 +3%
Throughput: +18% tokens/sec overall.

lina: That A100 p99 +40% is alarming. Any correlation with model size or KV behavior?

maya: Yes — digging into traces shows KV fragmentation and kernel switching during long batches. Example profiling line: `kv_miss_rate=0.18, kernel_switches=13, memcpy_ms=24`. When fragmentation > ~12% the runtime falls back to slower paths and we get memcpy storms.

simon: That implies kernel selection thrash. We should cap max_tokens_per_batch for A100 in SLO mode to avoid huge batches that trigger the fallback. My quick suggested caps: A100 48k, H100 64k, A10 36k, L4 24k, T4 16k.

ranjit: Caps look reasonable. We should make them model-aware too — some customers submit 32k prompts frequently. Also consider max_batch_items to bound kernel shapes.

maya: I prototyped a policy file (yaml) to test — dropping it here for visibility:

```yaml
policy: slo_packing_v1
per_accelerator:
  H100: {max_tokens_per_batch: 64000, max_batch_items: 32}
  A100: {max_tokens_per_batch: 48000, max_batch_items: 24}
  A10:  {max_tokens_per_batch: 36000, max_batch_items: 20}
  L4:   {max_tokens_per_batch: 24000, max_batch_items: 16}
  T4:   {max_tokens_per_batch: 16000, max_batch_items: 12}
kv_protection:
  fragmentation_threshold: 0.12
  throttle_on_flip: true
```

lina: Can we add an adaptive rule: if kv_miss_rate > fragmentation_threshold then reduce max_tokens_per_batch by 25% for the next 5 minutes (per-shard)?

simon: Also add a signal: if kernel_switches > 5/s then immediately reduce packing aggressiveness and emit an alert.

perf-bot: Experiment created: exp-2026-03-slo-packing-a100-cap, trial id=exp-2026-03-71, dashboard: https://ci.internal/exp/1234

maya: I'll run the shard-level sweep overnight with extra perf logging and stack samples. Please watch the dashboard for regressions in customer-facing routes and let me know if we should rollback the policy.

ranjit: Thanks — if we still see A100 tail issues tomorrow morning let's convene and iterate.
